title: Clarify unregistered-repo dispatch preflight and ensure derived lifecycle labels
body:
# Clear preflight and label initialization for config-free project worker dispatch

## What
Improve diagnostics and preflight for native issue-backed worker dispatch in an
existing Git repository that has not been registered with aidevops. Also ensure
that wrapper-derived lifecycle labels exist before issue creation requests them.

## Observed evidence
- Managed issue creation using `gh-write-helper.sh issue create` derived
  `status:available` even though that label did not exist. Creation failed with
  `could not add label: 'status:available' not found`. A subsequent exact bounded
  issue-list check proved no issue was created; after standard label creation,
  the same managed creation succeeded. No raw-creation fallback was used.
- `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch ... --base origin/<feature> --dry-run`
  reported dispatchable/clear dedup and exit 0. The real command failed before
  claim with `runner_capability_unmet source=fresh metadata_unreadable`.
- Reading `_dsi_check_runner_capability` showed that this particular message is
  emitted when `_dsi_repo_path_for_slug` returns no registered directory, before
  any fresh issue metadata check. The actual cause was absent repo registration,
  not unreadable issue metadata or provider authentication. No worker was launched.

## Why
Misleading dry-run/real-launch diagnostics waste model calls and encourage retries
or unauthorized registry changes. A clear bounded preflight should preserve the
guard and identify the missing bootstrap prerequisite without enabling automation.

## How
### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`

### Reference pattern
Installed helper `_dsi_repo_path_for_slug`, `_dsi_check_runner_capability`, and
`cmd_dispatch` dry-run branch; create-wrapper `_gh_ci_prepare_status_label` and
`gh_create_issue`. Expected source paths above; verify against current framework
HEAD before writing. Existing focused helper tests are not known: discover their
actual paths and record them through normal scope recovery if needed.

### Implementation
Give missing/unregistered/nonexistent canonical path a specific actionable reason,
distinct from fresh metadata failures. Make dry-run disclose this prerequisite
without claims, worktrees, repo registration, global config or worker launch. Keep
the fresh capability check at the real preclaim trust boundary; do not weaken any
auth/secret/ownership requirement. Ensure derived canonical status labels with the
existing label helper or fail with a correct bounded prerequisite diagnostic;
do not create arbitrary caller-supplied labels or bypass repository permissions.

### Verification
Use existing isolated helper tests/fixtures: unregistered repo, nonexistent path,
registered repo, fresh issue-metadata failure, new repo missing lifecycle labels,
label-create permission failure. Assert dry-run is non-mutating, real dispatch
remains fail-closed, reason codes distinguish causes, and no duplicate issues or
workers are produced. ShellCheck the changed scripts; no new runner or broad gate.

## Boundaries / rollback
No project/private repository identifiers, local paths or secrets in this report.
No registration/maintenance/schedule change or guard bypass. Reverse only this
focused diagnostic/preflight patch if a regression occurs. This is framework
repair, not authority to execute or merge any project task.

title: browser-qa-helper: transition command to measure a page while the next page loads (held navigation)
body:
## What

Add a `transition` command to `browser-qa-helper.sh` that checks what a page shows **while the next page is still loading**: click a link, hold the next document's response for a set time, measure the page (DOM geometry, chosen elements, frames painted) during the hold, then release it and report.

## Why

Loading placeholders, "instant" navigation feedback, skeletons and flash-of-unstyled-content fixes can only be verified in the window between the click and the next page's first paint. On a fast local site that window is a few milliseconds, so ordinary screenshots never see it, and the obvious Playwright approaches fail silently. This was needed while building a click-response placeholder for a WordPress plugin's admin screens (aligning loading dots with the tab text: target error under 1 px), and had to be hand-built in a throwaway script. Any project with route transitions, prefetch or speculation rules, or placeholder UI needs the same check.

## What was learned (the traps)

1. **Hold the right request.** Use `context.route('**/*')` and hold only `route.request().isNavigationRequest()` (resource type `document`) matching a URL pattern, then `route.continue()` after `--hold-ms`. Prefetch and speculation-rules prerender also fetch documents: log `resourceType()` and the time of every document request, or the "held" page may already be prerendered and the test silently measures the wrong thing.
2. **`page.evaluate()` cannot read the held state.** While a navigation is pending, it fails with "Execution context was destroyed" or waits until the next page commits, then measures the new page (all values `null`). A raw CDP session (`Runtime.evaluate`, `Page.captureScreenshot`) waited the same way.
3. **What works:** `context.addInitScript()` registers a capture-phase `click` listener that, after `--at-ms` (for example 600 ms), runs the measurement function in the page and `console.log`s `PREFIX + JSON.stringify(result)`; the runner collects it from `page.on('console')`. This reads the page exactly as the user sees it during the hold.
4. **Frames:** `Page.startScreencast` (CDP) frames, timestamped against the click, showed how many frames were painted before a given element (for example the footer) existed. That is the check for "no flash" / render-blocking fixes. Screenshots during the hold are unverified; screencast frames are the likely route.
5. Text position, not box position: measure text with `document.createRange().selectNodeContents(el).getBoundingClientRect()`; element boxes include padding.

## How (suggested)

- New `cmd_transition` in `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh` (dispatcher and `cmd_help`), with the script generator in a new `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-transition.sh` (sourced like `browser-qa-helper-tests.sh`), following `_generate_stability_script` (`browser-qa-helper.sh` ~line 170) for the `.mjs` temp file pattern (t2997: exact `.mjs` name in `mktemp -d`).
- Options: `--url BASE --from PATH --click SELECTOR --hold URL-SUBSTRING [--hold-ms 4000] [--at-ms 600,1200] --measure-file FILE.js` (a function returning JSON-able data) `[--storage-state FILE] [--screencast] [--format json|markdown] [--output-dir DIR]`.
- Report: document requests with type and time, navigation commit times, each measurement with its time, and with `--screencast` the frame count before release and frame images (max 1568 px, per the screenshot limits).
- Document it in `.agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md` with one example (a placeholder alignment check).
- Uses the shared Playwright runtime (`playwright-runtime.mjs`); no new installs.

## Acceptance

- Against a local test server whose second page is delayed: the measurement during the hold reads the first page (non-null values from a placeholder element added on click), and the report shows the held document request and the commit after release.
- With a page that prefetches the target, the report lists the prefetch request so a misleading run is visible.
- `--screencast` reports the number of frames painted during the hold.
- ShellCheck clean; `browser-qa-helper.sh help` lists `transition`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-transition.sh`
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md`

## Context

Observed 2026-10-08 in an interactive session; the throwaway script is not kept in any repository (paths unknown to workers: build from the description above).

title: GH#33997 follow-up: continue For #N orphan-recovery checkpoint drafts instead of a permanent dispatch hold
body:
## What

Make the pulse's own `For #N` orphan-recovery checkpoint drafts continuable, so a killed worker's issue reaches exact-head continuation instead of a permanent `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` hold. This carries the primary fix for #33997; its PR should use `Resolves #33997` alongside this issue.

## Why (root cause, verified against current main)

When a worker dies with a dirty worktree, `_handle_worker_branch_orphan` opens a draft titled `checkpoint: recover dirty worker worktree for #N`. It is labelled `origin:worker-takeover` and its body has a non-closing `For #N` line by design (GH#32933). See `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:621-629`. Three paths then disagree:

1. Dedup has-open-pr reports `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` for this draft, so ordinary redispatch is blocked and negative-cached.
2. Stale recovery (`_stale_recovery_find_open_pr` → `_stale_recovery_linked_pr_rows`, `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh:240-335`) only reads `closingIssuesReferences`. It does not see the draft. The proactive sweep (`_normalize_stale_open_pr_blocks_reset`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:132-145`) therefore resets the issue to `status:available`, unassigned, with no `CLAIM_RELEASED`.
3. Continuation rejects the draft: `_pr_checkpoint_pr_metadata_is_eligible` requires a closing link (`.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh:70`). `dispatch-stalled` also needs a stall release, which never exists (`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:786-791`).

Field evidence (#33997 comments, aidevops 3.38.29-3.38.31): each cycle logs `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED ... has no current stall release`, then `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`. Three issues were stuck for more than 50 minutes until manual intervention.

Correction to the #33997 review: its item 1 (sweep writes a stall release) assumed the sweep ignores drafts. It already skips closing-linked drafts, so that change alone fixes nothing for these `For #N` drafts. #34007 shipped item 2 (approval-template guard) only.

## Reproducer

**Causal status:** confirmed by code path on current main and by the field symptom in #33997.

1. A worker dispatched for issue N commits work and is then killed with a dirty worktree, so no release path runs (for example the #33993 cgroup kill, fixed in #34006).
2. Orphan recovery opens draft M: `checkpoint: recover dirty worker worktree for #N`, labelled `origin:worker-takeover`, with body `For #N`.
3. About 35 minutes later, the sweep logs `Stale assignment reset: #N ... no worker process`. It resets the issue to `status:available`, unassigned, and posts no `CLAIM_RELEASED`.
4. Every later cycle logs:

```
STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: PR #M in <repo> has no current stall release
BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_SKIPPED: PR #M in <repo> has no current blocked release
[dispatch_with_dedup] DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked signal=exact_head_continuation_unavailable issue=#N
```

5. A manual `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch` fails with `PR_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_BLOCKED ... not an open, unheld worker draft linked to issue #N`.

**Expected:** `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION: issue #N ... PR #M preserved for exact-head continuation`, followed by one bounded continuation launch.

## How (recommended; worker verifies and may refine)

- **Linkage, one rule:** treat a PR as exactly linked to issue N when it has a closing link, or when all of these hold:
  - `closingIssuesReferences` is empty
  - the body has an exact `^For #N` line (reuse the regex at `pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh:39-44`, which the signed revision path already uses)
  - it is a draft labelled `origin:worker-takeover`, not cross-repository, and carries none of the protected labels
- Apply that rule in both `_pr_checkpoint_pr_metadata_is_eligible` and `_stale_recovery_linked_pr_rows`. Stale recovery then classifies the draft as `draft_checkpoint`: the sweep skips reset and Layer 6 emits `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION` → `_dispatch_stale_pr_checkpoint_continuation` → `_pcc_dispatch`. No synthetic release is needed. Keep the `expected_author` check: the PR author is the runner that created the recovery draft.
- **Already-reset issues** (unassigned, no release, `For #N` draft): decide whether `dispatch-stalled` may accept "no trusted coordination event newer than the draft head, plus expired claim" as stall evidence. Keep the existing `stalls >= 2` attention bound. If it's unsafe, document the manual route instead.
- **Completion semantics:** the continuation must end in a PR that resolves the issue. Check whether the continuation worker rewrites `For #N` to a closing keyword when marking ready; if it does not, add that step.
- Out of scope: accepting `crash_during_execution` / `worker_failed` releases on `Resolves #N` drafts with `status:blocked`. Record it as a separate decision if it is still needed after this change.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh`

Functions: `_pr_checkpoint_pr_metadata_is_eligible` (or `pr-closing-link-lib.sh` if the rule belongs there), `_stale_recovery_linked_pr_rows` / `_stale_recovery_find_open_pr`, and `_pcc_dispatch_stalled` only if the already-reset case is accepted.

## Verification

- Extend the existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh` cases. Do not add a new harness.
  - A `For #N` `origin:worker-takeover` draft is accepted.
  - A `For #N` draft with the `origin:worker` label, a ready (non-draft) PR, a cross-repo PR, a protected label, a bare `#N` mention, or a closing link to another issue is still rejected.
  - Stale recovery classifies the accepted draft as `draft_checkpoint`, and the sweep skips reset.
- `shellcheck -x` on the changed scripts.
- Production signal: after a killed worker leaves a recovery draft, the pulse log shows `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION: issue #N ... PR #M preserved for exact-head continuation` within a cycle or two of the stale threshold, and no repeated `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`.

title: Flaky: bounded-operation forked-descendant test races 60ms budget (timed_out vs succeeded)
body:
## Description

`Plugin Import Check` (`import-check`, non-required) failed on release PR #34011, which changed only version and changelog files. The failing assertion is a timing race in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:416`:

```
not ok 8 - failure, timeout, and scoped cancellation cannot appear as success
  expected: 'timed_out'
  actual: 'succeeded'
  location: test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:393:3 (assert at 416:12)
```

The `forked` case starts a parent that spawns an unref'd child with inherited stdio, then exits immediately. It uses `budgetMs: 60`. Whether the manager observes the surviving descendant before it records the parent's exit as success depends on scheduling. The same workflow passed on the five previous runs, including release PR v3.38.31.

## Expected Behavior

The test should deterministically show that a parent that exits while leaving a live descendant cannot report `succeeded`. Its result must not depend on a 60 ms budget racing descendant discovery.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` (CI: `Plugin Import Check` → `Run plugin tests`)

**Actual output:** `not ok 8 - failure, timeout, and scoped cancellation cannot appear as success` with `expected: 'timed_out'`, `actual: 'succeeded'` (intermittent)

title: t18622: fix(pulse): detached script routine lock is never released, stalling every sc...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18622` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `priority:high`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): detached script routine lock is never released, stalling every script routine

## Done when

- [ ] After a detached script routine exits (success or failure), `${ROUTINE_STATE_FILE}.<id>.runner` no longer exists.
- [ ] A runner lock with no PID file or a dead PID, older than the grace period, is reclaimed and the routine runs on its next due cycle; a lock with a live owner PID is never removed.
- [ ] `routine-state.json` records a terminal status for each completed run; skipped dispatches do not leave a permanent `running` state.
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh` is clean.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:273-342` — fix trap expansion, record the owner PID, reclaim dead-owner locks
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-tracking-updates.sh` — existing test added by #32668 for this path; add one regression case for lock release and stale reclaim

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_routine_dispatch_script` (`pulse-routines.sh:309-342`) spawns `_routine_run_detached_script` via `setsid`/`perl`/`nohup bash -c`; `_routine_execute` (`pulse-routines.sh:348+`) calls the dispatcher. Nothing else reads `*.runner` (search: `rg -n '\.runner' .agents/scripts`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** only `_routine_run_detached_script` creates/removes `${ROUTINE_STATE_FILE}.${routine_id}.runner`. `_routine_update_state` and `_routine_record_lifecycle` write state and lifecycle.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-tracking-updates.sh` (from #32668).
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because the lock directory `${ROUTINE_STATE_FILE}.<id>.runner` is internal runtime state with no schema (searched: `rg -n '\.runner' .agents/scripts`).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed copy at `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`, updated by `setup.sh`/release.
- **Migrations/backfills:** existing leaked lock directories (`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/routine-state.json.<id>.runner`) hold no owner PID. Reclaim must treat a lock with no PID file, or a dead PID, as stale. That clears the 32 existing locks on the first post-deploy cycle without a manual step.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reverting `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh` restores the old behaviour; the lock remains a plain directory, removed only at its exact path.

### Implementation Steps

1. Expand the lock path when the trap is set, not when it fires. For example:

   ```bash
   # shellcheck disable=SC2064 # expand lock_dir now; the local is gone at EXIT
   trap "rmdir $(printf '%q' "$lock_dir") 2>/dev/null || true" EXIT
   ```

   Better still, release the lock explicitly after `_routine_finalize_terminal`, before `return 0`, and keep the trap only as a fallback for crashes. If a PID file is written inside the lock (step 2), use `rm -rf -- "$lock_dir"` scoped to that exact path instead of `rmdir`.
2. Record ownership: after `mkdir "$lock_dir"` succeeds, write `$$` to `"$lock_dir/pid"`. When `mkdir` fails, read `pid`. If it is missing or `kill -0` fails, and the lock is older than a short grace period (for example 60s, which covers the gap between `mkdir` and writing the PID), remove that exact lock path, log `routine <id>: reclaimed stale runner lock`, and retry `mkdir` once.
3. When the lock is held by a live owner, keep the current skip. Make sure the pre-dispatch `running` state written by `_routine_dispatch_script` is not left as the final record for a dispatch that never ran. Either check the lock in the dispatcher before writing `running`, or leave the existing state untouched on the skip path.
4. Run `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`, then the existing test.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** `mkdir` stays the atomic acquire. Reclaim removes only a lock whose recorded owner is dead (or which has no PID past the grace period) and retries `mkdir` once. A concurrent pulse that wins the retry keeps the lock.
- **Migration/rollback:** existing PID-less locks are reclaimed after the grace period. Rollback leaks locks again, as it does today.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** an old-version runner holding a PID-less lock and still alive (unlikely, given the 10-day age) would be reclaimed after the grace period. The grace period must be well below the routine cadence and above the `mkdir`→PID write gap.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a routine that genuinely runs long (r916 ~5 min) keeps its live-PID lock, so no double run happens.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** SIGKILL or a reboot leaves a lock with a dead PID, which is reclaimed on the next due cycle.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-tracking-updates.sh
# Production path after deploy: next pulse cycle should log completion, not "already active"
rg -n 'routine r916: (script completed|script exited|reclaimed stale)' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
```

- **Surface mapping:** shellcheck covers the trap quoting; the test covers lock release and stale reclaim; the pulse log proves the production path.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required; single module.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-tracking-updates.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `cloudron app packaging upstream version update routine` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 1 commit after #32668 touches `pulse-routines.sh` (af5e6017ec, unrelated backup work); 0 open PRs; no matching issues for "detached runner already active" or "routine lock"
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:273-342` present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — known bug with resolved fix; stale-lock reclaim policy is a small bounded choice
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — two-line root-cause fix plus reclaim; issue-only is sufficient

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-08
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** The user asked whether routines keep our Cloudron app packages current. r916 (Cloudron upstream check) has not run since 2026-09-28. The cause is a lock that affects every script routine.

## What

Script routines dispatched through `_routine_dispatch_script` must release their per-routine runner lock when the detached runner exits. They must also recover from a lock left by a runner that died. After the fix, each due script routine runs, records a terminal state (`success`, `failure` or `deferred`), and runs again at its next due time.

## Why

`_routine_run_detached_script` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:273-307`) acquires `lock_dir` with `mkdir`, then sets:

```bash
trap 'rmdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
```

`lock_dir` is a function-local variable, and the single-quoted trap expands it only when the shell exits. By then the function has returned and the local is gone. The trap runs `rmdir ""`, which fails silently, so the lock directory stays. Every later dispatch then logs `routine <id>: detached runner already active` and returns without running anything.

Evidence (this host, 2026-10-08):

- 32 empty lock directories `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/routine-state.json.<id>.runner` exist (r040-r046, r902-r920, r-pulse-check, r-session-miner, r-gh-audit-scan, r-keywords-*, r-issue-archive, r-attribution-scan). Most were created 2026-09-28 ~02:13 UTC, a few hours after #32668 merged (2026-09-27T22:20Z). No runner process is alive.
- `routine-state.json` shows `last_status: running` for all of them. For example, r916 has `last_run 2026-09-27T03:33:50Z` and `last_attempt 2026-10-07T22:19:52Z`.
- `pulse.log` repeats `routine r916 is due ... dispatching ... detached runner already active` on every cycle, about 4 times a day for 10 days.
- r917 completed a run on 2026-10-04 with `script exited with code 1` and finalized its state, but its lock directory from that run still exists. So a normal exit leaks the lock too, not only a crash.
- Minimal repro: a bash script whose function sets `local lock_dir=...; mkdir "$lock_dir"; trap 'rmdir "$lock_dir" ...' EXIT` leaves the directory after the script exits.

Impact: no script routine runs at all. That includes r916/r917, so Cloudron packages behind upstream have not had update issues filed since 2026-09-27: NetBird v0.80.0, AI DevOps Worker v3.38.33 and Buzz v0.5.27 are pending.

title: fix: batch pre-push privacy scans with custom inventories
body:
## Problem and observed evidence

The pre-push privacy guard exceeds short push budgets after incorporating a large upstream update. This was observed while preparing PR #33947; no hook was disabled and no NixOS package installation was attempted.

- SSH authentication succeeds and Git reaches the managed pre-push dispatcher.
- With `PRIVACY_GUARD_DEBUG=1`, the actual push comparison reports 11,698 diff lines and zero secret-material candidate lines, then remains in the public/private-entity scan. The push did not finish within a 120-second interactive bound.
- A diagnostic-only invocation comparing the same head against its current main base reports 115 diff lines and succeeds within a 30-second bound. This smaller comparison was not substituted for the actual push's remote baseline.
- The complexity guard passes all three metrics standalone; repo-verify passes its declared Bun typecheck standalone. Bash syntax checking succeeds and bash, git, gh, jq, timeout, ShellCheck, grep, awk, sed, python3, perl and bun are available. GNU grep and awk were exercised successfully. No evidence supports installing missing software.

Issue #31548 documents a previous repair introducing conservative candidate filtering while explicitly retaining full scans for custom inventories. In the current helper, `privacy_scan_public_diff` enables the fast path only when both private-entity and custom-path inventories are empty. Otherwise it calls `privacy_scan_public_text` once per added line; that launches several subprocesses for path and credential checks. This remaining path can still make large pushes look stalled. Actual personal inventories were not printed or copied; reproduce using synthetic configuration only.

## Desired outcome

Reduce large-diff overhead when custom inventories are present, without reducing the authoritative privacy coverage or encouraging routine hook bypass. This is a framework performance follow-up, not additional functionality for PR #33947 and not authority for release or catalogue publication.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-privacy-diff-fast-path.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`

Inspect `.agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh` and the existing candidate filter as reference patterns. Do not alter Git hook installation, NixOS configuration, target-publicity lookup, private data inventories, remote baseline selection or the PR #33947 dispatch changes.

## Implementation guidance

Profile the existing path using a synthetic nonempty entity inventory and a synthetic custom path rule. Prefer conservative batched candidate selection or equivalent batching that retains the current authoritative scanner. Never assume an ordinary-looking line is safe from arbitrary configured rules. If rules cannot be represented conservatively, retain an explicit safe fallback. Preserve literal matching, configured regex semantics, script-reference allowances, PEM state isolation, file/line attribution, error propagation and the existing protection against inventory changes during a scan. Do not emit private inventory values into diagnostics.

## Verification and acceptance

- Exercise the actual hook path against a synthetic large comparison with nonempty custom inventories; document before/after wall time and prove it completes without hook bypass. Use a session-owned disposable repository, not another user's checkout or real secrets.
- Run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-privacy-diff-fast-path.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`, plus scoped ShellCheck and the repository's changed-file gates.
- Extend existing regression coverage only: configured entity hits, configured path hits on otherwise ordinary lines, malformed/unreadable inventories, inventory changes, token prefixes, script-reference allowances and cross-file PEM state must preserve existing results.
- Show that ordinary large diffs no longer trigger repeated per-line subprocess work when custom inventories are active. State any retained full-scan fallback and its bounds; do not claim a completed scan from a timeout or absent output.
- Keep all privacy guards and merge/CI controls enabled. No new test runner, global package installation or unrelated changes.

title: Worker network policy intermittently denies the dispatched repo's Git origin; blocked release claims unpushed commits are preserved but they are lost
body:
## Observed

Three headless workers on one managed private repo released `permission_required` because the worker network policy denied **Git origin access** (remote discovery, fetch and push). Each worker reported its work as "preserved in a local commit". Other workers on the same runners and versions push to the same HTTPS origin without problems in the same period, and opened dozens of PRs on 2026-10-08.

| When (UTC) | Version | Runner | Worker statement |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-07 14:53 and 15:36 (2 attempts) | v3.38.23, OpenCode 1.15.10/1.18.34, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` | runner A | "runner policy denies the registered Git origin for both refresh and push", 2 unpushed commits |
| 2026-10-08 03:09 | v3.38.33, OpenCode 1.18.34 | runner A | "Push was denied by the runner network policy", 1 unpushed commit |
| 2026-10-08 05:55 | v3.38.33, OpenCode 1.18.34 | runner B | "Shared worker network policy denied Git origin remote discovery", 1 unpushed commit |

## Two defects

1. **Intermittent origin denial.** The registered origin of a pulse-managed repo is a required egress for every implementation worker. A policy or tier decision that denies it fails closed in the wrong place. The worker can never deliver, and it releases as `permission_required`, which waits on a human. Find which layer produced the denial: the sandbox egress profile, the network tier classification, or the OpenCode command policy. Find why it applies only to some sessions, for example a model/provider route, the egress mode `auto` resolving differently, or a remote-discovery command shape (`git remote -v`, `git ls-remote`) that is classified differently from `git push`.
2. **"Preserved" commits are lost.** On runner A, none of the reported commit SHAs exist in the canonical repository object store. No linked worktree, branch or recovery-store entry exists for those issues. The blocked-release path lets the worker claim preservation while worktree cleanup (or an isolated object store) discards the work. Source captures and ledgers had to be redone.

## Files Scope (candidates, exact path to be confirmed by reproduction)

- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/network-tier-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`

### Files Scope

Confirmed by reproduction (worker GH#34040). Every retained runner denial excerpt is the OpenCode command policy (`network.worker-policy`) reporting `unclassified worker network destination (git-push-destination-missing)` for a bare `git push`, while an explicit `git push origin <branch>` in the same session and worktree is allowed. The bare form resolves its default remote through `_default_git_remote` in the argv analyzer, which turns any failed or slow (5 s hard timeout) Git query into an anonymous denial. The blocked-release (`permission_required`) path never pushes or bundles the worker's local commits, and the abnormal-exit push fallback archives only uncommitted diffs.

- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_network.py`
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_git.py`
- `.agents/scripts/network-tier-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

- A worker session can always reach the registered origin of its dispatched repo (fetch, ls-remote, push of its own branch) under the default egress profile. Any denial is logged with the exact layer and rule.
- If push fails anyway, the release path verifies that the claimed commit exists in a durable location: pushed WIP ref, recovery bundle, or retained worktree with an owner marker. Otherwise it reports `work_lost` instead of claiming preservation.

## Verification

- Reproduce with a headless worker on the default egress profile that runs `git ls-remote origin` and `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<test-branch>` against an HTTPS GitHub origin, under each routed provider.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-network-egress.sh`
- After the fix, the three affected issues re-arm through `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`.

title: File-size gate: let root Markdown files grow to 1,000 lines, and try a conciseness pass before blocking
body:
## What

1. Raise the file-size gate for Markdown files in a repository's **root** (for example `AGENTS.md`, `STANDARDS.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`) from 500 to **1,000 lines**, so those documents have headroom. Markdown files below the root keep the 500-line limit; `README.md` stays exempt.
2. When any process hits the Markdown size limit (pre-push hook, `linters-local.sh`, the CI gate, or an agent/worker reading their output), it must first consider whether the **whole document** can be made more concise **without losing any detail** (repetition, wordiness, sections duplicated elsewhere, tables in place of prose), do that if it can, and only then fall back to splitting the file or a justified bypass (`complexity-bump-ok` / `COMPLEXITY_GUARD_DISABLE=1`).

## Why

Observed (owner session): a private plugin repository syncs core files word for word from an upstream starter template (`scripts/sync-core.sh`). The template's `STANDARDS.md` (repository root) grew from 500 to 554 lines in three commits. The sync PR could not push: the pre-push complexity guard blocked it with `REGRESSION: 1 new violation(s)` on `STANDARDS.md` (554 lines). The file cannot be shortened in the downstream repo (it must match the template), so the owner had to approve `COMPLEXITY_GUARD_DISABLE=1`. Root documents are the always-read entry points of a repository; 500 lines is too tight for them, and every downstream copy inherits the block.

The guard's output also misled diagnosis: the hook prints `file-size: .sh/.py files must be <= 1500 lines`, and `complexity-regression-helper.sh` documents `file-size` as ".sh and .py files over 1500 lines", while the check actually scans non-README Markdown over 500 lines (its report says so). Fix the messages in the same change.

## How

Files (verify each before editing; the limit is repeated):

- `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh` — the file-size scan (around line 394–432: `-gt 500`), the metric label (`file-size) printf 'non-README Markdown file(s) >500 lines'`, around line 588) and the header comment (line 21, stale ".sh and .py files over 1500 lines"). Use 1,000 for files with no `/` in their repo-relative path, 500 otherwise.
- `.agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh` — threshold message around line 213 (stale ".sh/.py files must be <= 1500 lines"); state both limits, and add one line of remediation: "First make the whole document more concise without losing detail; split or bypass only if that is not enough."
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` (`readonly MAX_FILE_LINES_BLOCK=500`, line 104; header comment line 94) and `.agents/scripts/linters-local-analysis.sh` (around lines 785–853, including the error text "Split/index before committing") — root limit 1,000, same conciseness-first remediation text.
- `.agents/scripts/file-size-regression-helper.sh` (`FILE_SIZE_DEFAULT_LIMIT=500`, line 53, and the report around line 341).
- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` (around lines 847–922) — same scope rule and messages.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-linters-local-complexity-gates.sh` (`MAX_FILE_LINES_BLOCK=500`, line 115) — update the expectation; add a case for a root Markdown file between 501 and 1,000 lines passing and a nested one failing.
- Docs: `.agents/tools/code-review/codacy.md` (line 48 table row), `.agents/reference/progressive-disclosure.md` or wherever the Markdown size policy is described, and the "Hook self-block" / bypass guidance, so agents read: conciseness pass first (no loss of detail), then split/index, then a justified bypass.

Reference pattern: the existing ratchet design (new violations only, `complexity-bump-ok` override) stays; only the per-path limit and the remediation order change.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A root Markdown file of 554 lines in a PR passes the pre-push guard, `linters-local.sh` and the CI file-size gate; at 1,001 lines it fails.
2. A Markdown file in a subdirectory still fails at 501 lines; `README.md` anywhere stays exempt.
3. The hook, local linter and CI messages state the real metric (Markdown, root 1,000 / elsewhere 500) and tell the reader to try a whole-document conciseness pass without loss of detail before splitting or bypassing.
4. Agent guidance (docs above) carries the same order, so a worker hitting the limit edits for concision before asking for a bypass.
5. ShellCheck clean; `.agents/scripts/tests/test-linters-local-complexity-gates.sh` passes.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh`
- `.agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local-analysis.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/file-size-regression-helper.sh`

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-file-size-regression-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/code-review/codacy.md`

title: OpenCode accepts daemonizing pulse dispatch in bounded operations, then loses worker liveness
body:
## Description

An OpenCode supervisor routed the supported `pulse-wrapper.sh --command dispatch` through `aidevops_bounded_operation`. Dispatch intentionally launches a detached worker, while the bounded tool owns and drains detached descendants when its command completes. The tool accepts this incompatible command instead of rejecting it before dispatch mutates ownership state. The launch receipt looked successful, but subsequent exact-issue checks found no worker and a stale in-progress label.

This report concerns command routing and lifecycle truthfulness. The descendant-cleanup protection itself is intentional and must remain enabled. All project identities, local paths, prompts, claims and lease values are omitted.

## Expected Behavior

- Reject known daemonizing worker-dispatch commands at the bounded-tool boundary before any claim or worker is created, with an actionable explanation of the supported launch route.
- Keep ordinary bounded commands, timeout/cancellation containment and detached test-server cleanup working.
- Supervisors must not equate command exit 0 or a dispatch receipt with durable worker liveness. Reconciliation must use exact-attempt ownership and normal trust gates, not manually remove an assignee or lease.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (project arguments intentionally replaced with placeholders):

```text
aidevops_bounded_operation.start({
  command: ["env", "PATH=<governed-helper-PATH>",
    "<installed-scripts>/pulse-wrapper.sh", "--command", "dispatch",
    "<issue>", "<owner/repo>", "<dispatch-title>", "<issue-title>",
    "<authenticated-login>", "<registered-repository-path>", "<worker-prompt>"],
  budget_seconds: 240,
  progress_interval_seconds: 30
})
```

**Actual output** (relevant receipt fields, with identifiers omitted):

```json
{"containment":"owned_process_tree","nested_process_groups":37,"state":"finalizing","elapsed_ms":110239,"budget_ms":240000,"remaining_ms":129761,"process_exit":0,"process_signal":null,"command_execution":"observed"}
{"containment":"owned_process_tree","nested_process_groups":37,"state":"succeeded","elapsed_ms":117435,"budget_ms":240000,"remaining_ms":122565,"process_exit":0,"process_signal":null,"command_execution":"observed"}
```

The worker's last startup log was at 12:05:46 UTC; the operation finalized at approximately 12:05:49 UTC. Subsequent PID checks found no worker or watchdog. Exact-issue status reported `No active dispatch`, while GitHub retained `status:in-progress`. The worktree had no implementation changes. The enclosing monitoring worker exited naturally later, at 12:08:14 UTC; that later exit is not established as the cause. The remaining budget rules out a recorded bounded-operation timeout.

**Expected output**: a prelaunch rejection of incompatible dispatch containment, with no new worker/claim, or a separately verified supported ownership handoff. Do not make detached workers exempt merely by dropping operation markers or weakening cleanup.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation for the historical worker's exact termination signal; confirmed code/test evidence for the incompatible containment contract and completion cleanup mechanism. No retained per-PID signal receipt establishes which signal killed that historical worker.

**Owning-path proof**:

- Entry point: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tools.mjs:250` binds `aidevops_bounded_operation` through `createBoundedInteractiveOperationTool`.
- Call chain: tool execute/start -> `BoundedInteractiveOperationManager.start` / `spawnOwned` -> bounded-operation supervisor -> `pulse-wrapper.sh --command dispatch` -> `dispatch_with_dedup` -> `_dlw_exec_detached` -> detached worker and observers. On command exit, the supervisor drains owned descendants, including nested process groups.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-tool.mjs:13-16` explicitly says commands must not daemonize or create a new process session.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-values.mjs:12-18` validates argv shape and size but does not reject this known daemonizing dispatch command.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1178-1220` starts the worker and detached observers.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs:141-149` initiates cleanup on successful command exit. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-process-tree.mjs:14-35` retains descendants across reparenting; `setsid` is not an ownership transfer.
- Integrated verification: the installed existing test `detached test servers are drained on completion, cancellation and expiry (GH#33747)` passed: 1 test, 0 failures, approximately 2.1 seconds. This confirms the supervisor mechanism, not an end-to-end proof of historical signal delivery.

**Causal code**:

```text
c3b6e74dfbbd3b2a757f196b591b0a11edf49b0e (merged PR #33753):
bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs:144-149 preserves command exit status
and starts cleanup when owned descendants remain after command exit.
```

This is attribution to the relevant cleanup path, not a claim that #33753's safety fix should be reverted. The same mechanism is still present in inspected local framework HEAD `3b68bb5050033d452990732edea339860db95605`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a controlled existing test fixture, use the bounded tool with a launcher that creates a detached long-lived child and exits 0. Do not create a real project issue or spend provider credits.
2. Observe that completion drains the child while reporting the launcher as succeeded; the existing detached-server test already covers this behavior.

title: Enforce PR-only worker authority before generic full-loop merge steps
body:
## What

Enforce a trusted PR-only/no-merge task boundary before a headless worker can execute a merge, rather than relying on the model to override the generic full-loop single-merge requirement. Stop at a verified PR for maintainer review; this brief does not authorize merge or deployment.

## Observed evidence

On aidevops 3.38.34 in OpenCode 1.18.35, an explicitly source/synthetic-only issue required delivery to a verified PR and no deployment/live operations. A trusted coordination comment additionally said **no merge**, and the canonical brief was clarified to say **do not attempt a merge** and to remove an inherited single-merge plan. The live worker nevertheless announced: "I'm publishing the source PR with those results and the operational limits, then making the required single gated merge attempt."

The parent paused the session-owned execution tree, cancelled the verified model runtime and took over final verification. The committed source was preserved, remote checks passed, and fresh readback showed an open, unmerged PR. The native dispatch then ended. No private repository names, issue/PR identifiers, source content, customer data or credentials are included in this report.

This demonstrates an announced authority conflict and missing pre-execution protection, not a completed unauthorized merge or proof that any particular lower-level helper already executed one. A later clarifying comment alone did not establish worker consumption. The original PR-only brief also must remain authoritative even when no later amendment is consumed.

## Investigation and write scope

- Inspect `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` for the appended generic full-loop lifecycle contract.
- Inspect `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`, `headless-runtime-launch.sh` and `headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh` for brief transport and owned-worker authority propagation.
- Inspect the existing GitHub operation permission/merge enforcement layer. Its exact runtime source path and existing regression-test paths are **not established** by this observation; discover them before proposing edits.
- Repair the narrowest existing authority enforcement surface. No new orchestrator, blanket model-permission enlargement, provider bypass, live GitHub reproduction, or weaker trust/approval policy.

## Required behavior

1. Trusted per-task PR-only/no-merge scope takes precedence over generic full-loop lifecycle text, including maintained repositories and green CI.
2. Deterministic enforcement blocks an unauthorized merge before a provider write even if the model plans one, bypasses prose, or does not consume a later clarification.
3. Preserve separately authorized merge workflows; never infer merge authority from issue dispatch, source approval, CI success, author ownership or a request to keep working.
4. Refusing only the merge path must not discard committed work or stall scoped source verification and ready-PR delivery.
5. Keep authority bound to the exact task/PR/owner and report the effective terminal boundary accurately.

## Verification

Use the existing synthetic permission/dispatch tests and local fakes. Cover a PR-only brief conflicting with generic single-merge instructions, a later trusted clarification, green-CI/no-merge, stale or missing authority, explicit scoped merge permission, and preservation of ready-PR/source work after a merge refusal. No new test infrastructure or actual merge/deployment is required. Include concrete target files, reference pattern and focused checks in the delivered PR.

## What

`cloudron-package-helper.sh preflight-release` reads the second whitespace field of every Dockerfile `FROM` line as the image reference. When a stage uses a flag, such as `FROM --platform=linux/amd64 image@sha256:...`, the flag is validated as an image and preflight fails with "Docker source must use an immutable tag-and-digest reference: --platform=linux/amd64". ## Reproducer

Observed by a worker on a Cloudron package upgrade PR (marcusquinn/cloudron-buzz-app#89). body:
## What

Make `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` follow `reference/ci-gate-policy.md` design rule 14 (#34084): on a credit-limited repository, a qlty check that fails because the credits ran out is reported as skipped, not as a terminal failure.

## Why

On an organisation repository, `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait <PR> --all` exited 1 with `FAIL: required checks reached a terminal failure` because of this check alone (`gh pr checks <PR> --json name,state,bucket,description,link`):

```json
{"bucket":"fail","description":"Qlty did not run because you are out of minutes.","name":"qlty check","state":"ERROR"}
```

Every other check passed. The agent had to work out by hand that this was billing, not code. Rule 14 says to skip such a failure, merge when the other checks pass, and note the skipped check in the PR body.

## How

Files to modify:

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
  - `canonicalize_checks()` (around line 234): keep `description` in the canonical check object. It is dropped today, and `gh pr checks --json` already returns it (check that the fetch requests the `description` field too).
  - `classify_state()` (around line 327) and `emit_failure_details()` (around line 371): treat a check as `skipping` when its name matches qlty case-insensitively (`qlty check`, not `Qlty Regression Gate`, which is a GitHub Actions job), its bucket is `fail`, and its description matches `out of minutes|out of credits`. Only do this when the repository is credit-limited: private, or owned by an organisation (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo} --jq '.private, .owner.type'`, read once per wait and cached). On a public personal-account repository, keep it a failure and print a note that this is unexpected.
  - Print one line per skipped check, for example `SKIPPED (qlty out of credits): qlty check <link>`, so callers can copy it into the PR body.
- Add a matching Bash 3.2-compatible test beside the existing helper tests (`git ls-files '.agents/scripts/tests/*checks-wait*'` to find them; if there are none, follow `.agents/scripts/tests/test-ci-failure-pattern-detection.sh`). Use stubbed `gh` output for the private-or-organisation case (skip) and the public personal-account case (still fail).

Reference pattern: `ci-infra-signature-lib.sh` (`CI_BILLING_OUTAGE_PATTERN`) is the existing billing-outage classifier for GitHub Actions annotations. Keep the qlty pattern separate, because qlty reports through a commit status description, not Actions annotations.

Out of scope: `full-loop-helper.sh merge` already ignores non-required checks, and pulse CI-repair routing (`pulse-merge-feedback-ci-patterns.sh`) matches by check name only. Note in the PR whether pulse would route a worker to this failure, and file a separate issue if it would.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`: zero findings.
- The new test passes for both cases.
- On an organisation-repository PR whose only failure is the qlty out-of-minutes status, `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait <PR> --repo <owner/repo> --all` exits 0 and prints the SKIPPED line.

Briefs that passed local `verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness` failed in CI's `planning-publication-reconcile.sh`. v3.34.12 also requires a `Tests/fixtures` write-surface field, and its Files Scope parser rejects `[slug]`-style path segments. Five issues stayed in `publication:pending` with no auto-dispatch until the briefs were patched to satisfy the older validator.

## Expected Behavior

After an upgrade, one documented command updates a pinned caller to the new tag. Options include:

- letting `--force-ref` and/or `--ref` act on `CURRENT/CALLER` rows whose `@ref` differs from the target, or adding a dedicated `--bump-pins`;
- having `check-workflows` report pin lag, for example `CURRENT/CALLER (pinned @v3.34.12; installed v3.38.35)`, so the lag is visible.

If pin bumping is intentionally out of scope, the template comment (and the matching comments in the other caller templates) should stop promising it and name the real procedure, which is editing the `uses:` refs and the matching `aidevops_ref` inputs by hand.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (downstream repo whose `issue-sync.yml` is byte-identical to the template apart from `runner:`, pinned to `@v3.34.12`, local install v3.38.35):

```bash
aidevops check-workflows --repo <owner>/<repo>
aidevops sync-workflows --repo <owner>/<repo> --workflow issue-sync --force-ref --ref @v3.38.35
```

**Actual output**:

```text
  [issue-sync] <owner>/<repo>                    CURRENT/CALLER   local evidence; ...
[sync-workflows-helper.sh] no actionable repos/workflows (all CURRENT or NO-WORKFLOW).
```

**Expected output**: a dry-run plan to rewrite the four `v3.34.12` refs to `v3.38.35`, or at least a `check-workflows` note that the pin lags the installed version.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `aidevops sync-workflows` → `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` main → actionable-row selection.
- **Call chain**: `check-workflows-helper.sh` normalises the reusable `@ref` before comparing (`_normalise_reusable_ref`, `check-workflows-helper.sh:225`; header line 17 "byte-identical to canonical (up to @ref pin variance)"), so a lagging pin classifies as `CURRENT/CALLER`. In `sync-workflows-helper.sh`, Step 1 of actionable selection keeps only `DRIFTED`, `NEEDS-MIGRATION` (and `NO-WORKFLOW`/`LOCAL_ONLY` with `--install-missing`) (around lines 806-819 on `main`). Step 2 re-admits `CURRENT/CALLER` rows only when `_needs_runner_sync` or the contributing-policy check fires (around lines 826-850). Nothing re-admits them for `@ref` lag, so execution ends at `no actionable repos/workflows` (line 1656). `_resolve_effective_ref` (around line 985) would apply `--force-ref`, but it is only reached for selected rows, and it only special-cases `DRIFTED`.
- **Integrated verification**: the dry-run above against a real downstream repo on v3.38.35 (latest), reproduced after confirming the same selection logic is on `main`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a managed downstream repo, pin `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` to an older tag, changing both `uses:` refs and both `aidevops_ref` inputs, and leave the rest byte-identical to the template.
2. Upgrade the local install to a newer version.
3. Run `aidevops check-workflows`: it reports `CURRENT/CALLER` and doesn't mention the lag.
4. Run `aidevops sync-workflows --workflow issue-sync --force-ref --ref @<new-tag>`: it reports `no actionable repos/workflows`.

## Workarounds Applied

1. Patched five task briefs to satisfy the older pinned validator (added `Tests/fixtures`; replaced a `services/[slug].astro` scope entry with its parent directory) so planning publication could reconcile.
2. Edited the four refs in `issue-sync.yml` by hand (switched to `@main` on the maintainer's choice), because `sync-workflows` could not do it.

Possible sibling (not filed): the local `verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness` and the CI-pinned reconcile can disagree whenever pins lag. A readiness check aware of the caller's pinned version, or a warning at publish time, would surface that before merge.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.38.35 (latest 3.38.35)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **AI Model**: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.100.0 (2026-09-03)

## Additional Context

Related but distinct: #20727 (review-bot-gate helper-SHA pin went stale; resolved by moving to reusable workflows, which doesn't cover tag-pinned callers) and #20649 (the original `sync-workflows` design, which deliberately preserves pins for `DRIFTED` rows).

title: docs(cloudron): OOM triage — 'mysql out of memory' can be host-wide OOM; fix version lookup
body:
## What / Why

Cloudron's "Out of memory: mysql service" notification (and `eventlog` `app.oom` for the `mysql` container) tells you to "consider increasing the memory limit". On an overcommitted host, that advice is misleading. In a production audit (Cloudron 10.0.5, 16 GB RAM, 47 apps), every MySQL kill was a **host-wide** OOM: kernel `constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE ... global_oom`, swap 100% full. mysqld was simply the largest process. The MySQL service limit had already been raised to 12 GiB, which did nothing. The trigger was the nightly `tgz` backup (a backup task with up to 2 GB of heap, plus Nextcloud data read over CIFS) running on top of about 20 GB of container RAM+swap demand.

`services/hosting/cloudron.md` currently only says ``Exited (137)` | OOM/SIGKILL | `dmesg | grep -i oom`, check memory limits``, which leads agents to the same wrong fix.

A second inaccuracy in the same file: the "Version" row reads `.version` from the box `package.json`, which returned `9.0.0` on a 10.0.5 server. The plain-text `VERSION` file beside it, in the same box directory, is correct.

## Proposed change

In `.agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md` (Troubleshooting), add a short "OOM triage" subsection:

- Tell the two OOM kinds apart: `journalctl -k | grep -E "oom-kill:constraint"`. `CONSTRAINT_MEMCG` with `oom_memcg=/docker/<id>` means the container hit its own limit, so raise that limit. `CONSTRAINT_NONE`/`global_oom` means the host ran out of memory, so raising the victim's limit does not help.
- Measure real per-container demand including swap: the cgroup v2 files `memory.current` and `memory.swap.current` in each container's `docker/<id>` cgroup directory. `docker stats` excludes swap.
- Correlate OOM times with tasks: box DB `tasks` (type `backup_*`, `creationTime`/`ts`) and `eventlog` `action='app.oom'`. Backup site memory limit: `backupSites.limitsJson`.
- Map container/DB IDs to apps: `apps` joined to `locations` (`type='primary'`), and `appAddonConfigs` (`CLOUDRON_MYSQL_DATABASE`).

Fix the Version row to read the box directory's `VERSION` file instead of `package.json`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md`

## Verification

- `rg -n "CONSTRAINT_NONE|memory.swap.current|box/VERSION" .agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md` finds the new guidance.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` passes (markdown).

title: Bug: Worker treats undiscovered pytest/Ruff tooling as an opaque permission blocker
body:
## Description

A source-only Python/Node worker repeatedly stopped with missing pytest/Ruff,
then classified the situation as `permission_required` because its brief forbade
dependency installation. The host already had an isolated verification environment
with both tools. The GitHub-visible terminal record did not identify the desired
operation, and the issue diagnostic showed zero recorded permission/blocker events.
The operator had to request another investigation to learn what permission was
supposedly needed. No concrete pending approval dialog was found.

Private repository identities, source filenames, local paths, session identifiers,
request tokens and raw telemetry are intentionally omitted.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:**
`pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue <issue> --repo <managed-repo>`

**Actual output:**

```text
Worker progress blockers:
  Retained events: 0
  Currently active: 0
  Reasons: {}
  (no blocker records found for this issue)
Result counts:
  - blocked: 4
```

The same issue's latest terminal release declares `permission_required` without
identifying the desired installation operation. Private identifiers are redacted
in the command above; the output counts are actual observations, not fixtures.

**Expected output:** a sanitized desired operation and whether a permission request
exists, together with evidence of the selected interpreter/tooling and safe
alternatives. The existing tools' successful version checks are reproduced below.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation of worker toolchain selection;
the reporting gap and successful existing-tool version checks are confirmed.

### Observed sequence

1. A worker task requires pytest, Ruff and normal pre-push hooks, and explicitly
   forbids dependency installation and hook bypasses.
2. An existing, approved isolated verification environment contains the tools,
   but it is not selected by the worker's interpreter/PATH lookup.
3. The worker concludes the tools are absent and emits
   `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=permission_required`. Four attempts ended blocked
   according to the issue diagnostic; the latest repeated the tooling explanation.
4. The issue-visible release reports only:

   ```text
   Terminal blocker: reason=permission_required owner=permission-maintainer
   Projected state: status:available.
   Raw evidence remains in protected worker telemetry.
   ```

5. `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue <issue> --repo <managed-repo>` reports
   `Retained events: 0`, `Currently active: 0` and no blocker records for this issue.
6. Targeted inspection of the final worker text reveals that the desired operation
   was dependency installation, not production access or protected-source access.
7. Non-mutating host checks against the already existing environment succeed:

   ```text
   <approved-verification-venv>/bin/python -m pytest --version
   pytest 8.4.2
   <approved-verification-venv>/bin/python -m ruff --version
   ruff 0.16.10
   ```

8. The operator authorized restarting with these existing tools. A normal manual
   dispatch from the preserved exact checkpoint launched successfully. No package
   was installed, permission broadened, or hook disabled. This is launch evidence,
   not yet proof that the resumed worker's verification completes successfully.

## Expected Behavior

- A missing executable on the current PATH should not become evidence that the
  dependency is uninstalled. Prefer an explicitly approved existing verification
  environment, record the selected interpreter and command-local PATH, and retain
  required checks. Do not scan arbitrary protected directories or install packages.
- Distinguish environment/tool discovery from an actual denied capability or a
  genuinely unavailable tool that requires new installation authority.
- A terminal-only permission report should include a sanitized, actionable desired
  operation and checked alternatives. It should say whether an actual request exists.
  An operator should not need raw telemetry just to learn what they are asked to
  approve. Preserve protected details and all exact-context permission checks.
- Preserve checkpoint work and bounded recovery. Do not repeatedly launch workers
  that receive unchanged failure evidence, fabricate grants or treat scheduling
  consent as capability approval.

## Error Output

Sanitized excerpt of the worker's final explanation:

```text
BLOCKED: Required pytest/Ruff tooling is still absent. Repairing that environment
requires dependency installation, which the unchanged trusted brief expressly
prohibits. Retrying does not grant that operation, and the pre-push gate cannot
be bypassed.
TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=permission_required
```

## Causal Status and Relevant Paths

The vague terminal projection and presence of reusable host tools are confirmed.
The precise worker interpreter/PATH choice and availability inside its isolated
runtime still need investigation; this report does not claim a global Ruff binary
was on that worker's PATH or that all missing-tool failures are false.

Installed source paths that appear relevant, expressed as repository paths:

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`: terminal reason instructions.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`: final-text blocker capture.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`: terminal-only permission projection;
  `_hrff_apply_terminal_permission_hold` explicitly distinguishes a terminal-only
  denial from an actual scoped request envelope.
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: generic terminal observation text.
- `.agents/hooks/repo-verify-pre-push.sh`: bare tool execution and selected toolchain.
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`: operator-facing blocker diagnosis.

Additional toolchain-discovery ownership is not yet established. Existing blocker,
headless-runtime and pre-push fixtures should be sufficient to exercise approved
existing-tool reuse, true missing tools, true denied permissions, report redaction,
and unchanged safety gates without paid model runs or live permission changes.

## Environment

- OS: macOS; shell: zsh with framework shell helpers.
- Assistant/runtime: OpenCode 1.18.35.
- Worker release comments: aidevops 3.38.36 and 3.38.37.
- Interactive CLI during recovery: 3.38.37, reporting agents 3.38.35.
  No update was performed during this investigation.
- Verified existing tooling: pytest 8.4.2 and Ruff 0.16.10.

## Third-party Tool Involvement

Python virtual-environment selection and PATH discovery only. No external-service,
credential or production integration was involved in the stated tooling blocker.

## Additional Context / Duplicate Check

Related closed issues: #31372 (in-worktree dependency-source provisioning) and
#30576 (capability fields dropped from a captured permission event). This report
concerns already installed Python verification tooling and a terminal-only report
with no captured permission event, rather than those exact prior paths. Searches
for Ruff/PATH worker failures and permission/tooling reports found no matching open
issue. Please consolidate if this is already covered by another current change.

- [x] Recorded observed versions rather than claiming an unverified latest version.
- [x] Removed private project names, paths, tokens and raw worker telemetry.

title: aidevops secret set truncates multi-line secrets (PEM keys) and leaks remaining lines to the shell
body:
## What

`aidevops secret set NAME` cannot store multi-line values such as PEM private keys (GitHub App keys, SSH keys, TLS keys). Add a safe multi-line path, for example `aidevops secret set NAME --from-file PATH` and/or full stdin when stdin is not a TTY. Reject or warn on multi-line pastes at the interactive prompt.

## Why (observed 2026-10-09)

A user stored a GitHub App private key with `aidevops secret set WPALLSTARS_RUNNERS_APP_KEY` and pasted the PEM at the hidden prompt.

- The TTY branch of the value reader in `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` (around lines 444–460) uses `IFS= read -rs value`. It consumed only the first line, `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----`, and stored that fragment as the secret.
- The remaining key lines went to the interactive shell, which tried to run them as commands. That exposed the private key in the terminal scrollback and possibly in shell history.
- The key had to be revoked and regenerated on GitHub. The workaround was `gopass insert --force aidevops/NAME < key.pem`, which bypasses the helper's validation and messaging.

This is a credential-exposure path in the documented "paste at hidden prompt" flow. It will recur for any PEM, JSON service-account key or other multi-line secret.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`, `cmd_set` and the value reader:
   - add `--from-file PATH`. Read the regular file exactly, refuse symlinks and world-readable files (warn at least), and keep the trailing newline handling consistent for PEM;
   - when stdin is not a TTY, read all of stdin, not just one line;
   - in TTY mode, after `read -rs`, drain any pending input with a short non-blocking read loop. If extra lines arrive, discard them without echoing, do **not** store the fragment, and print guidance to use `--from-file`. This stops the leftover lines reaching the shell.
2. Make sure the credentials.sh fallback stores multi-line values safely, quoted, or refuses them with guidance.
3. Update `aidevops secret help` and `reference/secret-handling.md` to document the multi-line route, including deleting the source file afterwards.

## Verification

- Store a generated test key with `--from-file` and from piped stdin. Check that `aidevops secret NAME -- sh -c 'printf "%s\n" "$NAME" | openssl pkey -noout -check'` prints `Key is valid`.
- Paste a multi-line value at the interactive prompt: nothing reaches the shell, nothing is stored, and the guidance is printed.
- ShellCheck stays clean on `secret-helper.sh`.
